Ernest Rutherford was a physicist born in 1871 at Brightwater, near Nelson, in New Zealand, who discovered the atomic nucleus. He is called the father of nuclear physics.

A scholarship took him from Canterbury College to Cambridge. In Canada he showed that radioactivity is the decay of atoms, winning the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1908. In Manchester in 1911 he showed that an atom has a tiny, dense nucleus.

In 1917 he changed one element into another, splitting the atom. As head of the Cavendish Laboratory he trained many physicists, and his work led to nuclear fission. He appears on the New Zealand $100 note. See nuclear-free New Zealand and Marie Curie.
sum: Ernest Rutherford was a physicist born in 1871 at Brightwater, near Nelson, in New Zealand, who discovered the atomic nucleus. He is called the father of nuclear physics.
